facts.statement: Koumpiodontosuchus was an extinct neosuchian crocodyliform that lived in the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England.
facts.quote: Koumpiodontosuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform from the Early Cretaceous Wessex Formation of England.

facts.statement: The first fossilized skull fragment of Koumpiodontosuchus was discovered by Diane Trevarthen on a beach near Sandown on the Isle of Wight in March 2011.
facts.quote: The first fossilised fragment of a skull was discovered by Diane Trevarthen on a beach near Sandown on the Isle of Wight in March 2011

facts.statement: A second skull fragment was found by Austin and Finley Nathan three months after the first discovery.
facts.quote: Three months later, the second fragment of the skull was found by Austin and Finley Nathan.

facts.statement: Megan Jacobs discovered an isolated tooth of Koumpiodontosuchus that was twice the size of the holotype teeth.
facts.quote: Megan Jacobs also discovered an isolated tooth belonging to the same genus that was twice the size of those from the holotype.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Steve Sweetman initially identified the fragments as belonging to Bernissartia fagesii due to their small size and button-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: When the fragments were first seen by Steve Sweetman, a palaeontologist with the University of Portsmouth, he thought that they belonged to the species Bernissartia fagesii because of its small size and button-shaped teeth.

facts.statement: Sweetman and colleagues named and described the new species in a 2015 paper published in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica.
facts.quote: In 2015, Sweetman and colleagues published a paper on the discovery of the new species in Acta Palaeontologica Polonica, where they named and described it.

facts.statement: The family Bernissartiidae, containing Koumpiodontosuchus, is recovered as the sister group to Eusuchia.
facts.quote: This group was recovered as the sister to Eusuchia.

facts.statement: Koumpiodontosuchus lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Koumpiodontosuchus is classified within the family Bernissartiidae.

rejected.statement: The species was named Koumpiodontosuchus aprosdokiti, which means 'unexpected button-toothed crocodile'.
rejected.quote: The species that the fragments belonged to was named Koumpiodontosuchus aprosdokiti, meaning 'unexpected button-toothed crocodile'.

rejected.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Koumpiodontosuchus as the sister taxon to Bernissartia within the family Bernissartiidae.
rejected.quote: This placed the genus as the sister taxon to Bernissartia within the family Bernissartiidae.
